headline: High: shared project-directory writes and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads the project directory by default, and its self_isolation is none; Agent B also reads/writes files and builds on shared context. That shared filesystem bridge makes prompt injection via file content plausible even without a direct parser claim. The interaction is documented in both profiles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF either agent consumes instructions from files in the shared project directory without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is run in the same workspace, file-based instruction smuggling can occur.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different project directories.
Disable automatic execution of file-sourced instructions.
Add a provenance banner to shared files before handoff.
Review any generated markdown or prompt files before B reads them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has broad network egress and handles OPENAI_API_KEY; Agent B has allowlisted egress and also reads/writes workspace files. Both touch shared project data, so generated source code or adjacent secrets can flow into outbound API calls. The profiles do not prove secret exposure by default, but the shared workspace plus egress makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF secrets or sensitive source files are placed in the shared project directory, either agent can read them.
IF either agent forwards file contents to its configured model/API, those contents may leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory.
Use separate API keys and principals for each agent.
Restrict outbound domains for both agents.
Redact sensitive files before either agent reads them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the same project directory and both support multiple instances, while Agent A explicitly shares state via the project directory. That creates a default write-conflict risk on generated code and artifacts even though neither profile mentions git locking or optimistic concurrency. Uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory concurrently, writes can overwrite each other.
IF either agent regenerates files while the other is editing them, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Assign disjoint subdirectories to each agent.
Take a quick backup before concurrent runs.
Use a file lock or manual handoff protocol.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a code generator that writes files then offers to run them, while Agent B’s skills build on shared context. That makes A’s output a likely input to B without a documented verification step. The pair can therefore propagate incorrect code or assumptions across work products, though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF B consumes A's generated files as authoritative context, errors can cascade.
IF A-generated code is reused by B without review, incorrect assumptions can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require B to cite file hashes or line references.
Run a quick diff against the previous version before handoff.
Reject outputs that lack explicit verification markers.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A is open-source coding tooling with generated source code and broad egress; Agent B is marketing tooling touching marketing content and product marketing context. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, and no PHI/PII class is stated. The only concrete compliance concern is a generic documentation gap, so low fits.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent's workspace, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployments, a policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention settings for each workspace.
Confirm data residency before deployment.
Add a short compliance checklist to the runbook.
